skill.name: migration
skill.description: Plan reversible, compatibility-safe migrations for schemas, data, APIs, protocols, configurations, and dependencies.
skill.summary: Design migration paths that preserve data, support rollback, and remain safe during mixed-version operation.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: The skill contains prompt-only guidance for reversible migrations and no executable code. No static or semantic security findings were identified.

content.value_statement: Complex migrations can lose data or break compatibility during staged rollouts. This skill structures transitions around preservation, verification, rollback, and mixed-version safety.
actual_capabilities: Maps current readers, writers, data shapes, ownership, and compatibility windows before changes.
Defines forward and rollback paths for schema, data, API, protocol, configuration, and dependency migrations.
Sequences compatible transitions through expansion, migration, verification, and contraction stages.
Plans safe mixed-version operation during overlapping rollouts.
Makes retries idempotent and partial failures observable.
Separates destructive contraction from earlier stages and requires explicit authorization.
limitations: Does not execute migrations, deployment commands, or rollback procedures.
Does not inspect systems unless relevant architecture, data flows, and constraints are provided.
Cannot guarantee preservation without representative tests, backups, and production evidence.
Does not replace database, infrastructure, security, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Evolve a Database Schema
use_cases.description: Plan an expand-and-contract schema change that supports old and new application versions.

use_cases.title: Transition an API Contract
use_cases.description: Stage an API change while preserving existing clients and defining measurable retirement criteria.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a Critical Dependency
use_cases.description: Design a reversible dependency upgrade with compatibility checks, staged rollout, and rollback triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this migration: [change]. Include prerequisites, forward steps, verification, and rollback.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the transition is defined but needs a safe execution sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Mixed-Version Compatibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [change] while versions [old] and [new] run together. Identify compatibility risks, mitigations, and exit criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for rolling deployments where readers and writers update at different times.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Expand-and-Contract Transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Design expand, migrate, verify, and contract stages for [change]. Define invariants, idempotent retries, observability, and rollback boundaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for schema or contract changes that require staged adoption.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Migration Preservation Proof
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [architecture and change]. Map readers, writers, ownership, failure modes, tests, rollback triggers, and evidence required before each stage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for high-impact transitions requiring reviewable safety evidence.

output_examples.input: Migrate customer status from free text to a controlled value set.
output: Expand: add the controlled status field while retaining the original field.
Migrate: backfill recognized values idempotently and quarantine unknown values.
Verify: compare counts, unknown values, and read behavior before switching.
Contract: remove the original field only after rollback is no longer required.

output_examples.input: Replace API field account_name with display_name during a rolling deployment.
output: Readers accept display_name first and fall back to account_name.
Telemetry confirms old clients have left the compatibility window.
Removal requires separate approval after rollback criteria expire.

output_examples.input: Upgrade a shared authentication dependency across several services.
output: Inventory consumers, supported versions, and authentication behavior before rollout.
Deploy to a small service cohort with error-rate and login-success checks.
Pause or roll back when predefined authentication thresholds fail.
Complete rollout only after every service passes compatibility verification.

best_practices: Document readers, writers, owners, invariants, and compatibility windows before changing production behavior.
Use idempotent steps with observable checkpoints and explicit rollback triggers.
Authorize destructive contraction separately after preservation and compatibility evidence passes.
anti_patterns: Do not combine expansion, migration, and destructive cleanup into one irreversible release.
Do not assume all services, clients, or workers update simultaneously.
Do not treat deployment success as proof of data preservation or behavioral compatibility.

faq.question: What migration types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports schema, data, API, protocol, configuration, and dependency transitions.

faq.question: Does this skill run migration commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning and implementation guidance but does not execute commands.

faq.question: How does it support rollback?
faq.answer: It defines rollback paths, triggers, boundaries, and required evidence before destructive stages.

faq.question: Can it plan rolling deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It considers mixed-version readers and writers throughout the compatibility window.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the current architecture, data shape, readers, writers, constraints, rollout process, and desired end state.

faq.question: When should contraction begin?
faq.answer: Begin only after verification passes, rollback needs expire, and destructive cleanup receives separate authorization.
